questions.question: Temperate grasslands are ideal for ______ cultivation.
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **wheat**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__****Grassland :**

 
• Grassland can be defined as a region where grasses form the dominant type of plant life.
 
• Grasslands make up almost a quarter of the total land surface. 
 
• We can divide the world’s grasslands into two broad categories: those that occur in the temperate region and those that occur in the tropical regions.

**​Explanation:**

Temperate grasslands:

 
• These are found in the mid latitudinal zones and in the interior part of the continents.
 
• Usually, the grass here is short and nutritious.
 
• Temperate grasslands are ideal for grain cultivation.
 
• The grasslands provide fertile soil, adequate rainfall, and favorable temperatures for the growth of grains such as wheat, barley, oats, and rye.
 
• Wild buffaloes, bison, antelopes are common in the temperate region.
 
• Temperate grasslands are composed of a rich mix of grasses and forbs and are underlain by some of the world’s most fertile soils.
 
• Since the development of the steel plough, most have been converted to agricultural lands.
 
• The temperate grasslands of North America are known as the Prairies.
 
• It is a region of flat, gently sloping, or hilly land.
 
• For the most part, prairies are treeless but, near the low-lying plains, flanking river valleys, and woodlands can be found. 
 
• It is actually a “sea of grass.”
 
• The temperate grasslands of South Africa are called the velds.
 
• Temperate Grasslands of Argentina are called Pampas.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

options.text: Metals are used in making cookware.
Metals are used in the manufacture of automobiles.
Living beings inhale metals during respiration.
Metals are used in manufacturing jewellery.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Living beings inhale metals during respiration**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__****Metallic Properties:**

__
 
• Metals are good conductors of heat and electricity.
 
• Metals are malleable and can be easily converted into thin sheets.
 
• Metals are ductile, which means they can be drawn into wires.
 
• They produce a ringing sound, which is why they are called sonorous. 
 
 
• Hence they are used in making school bells.
 
 
 
• They have a very high density.
 
• Metals have high melting points.
 
• Metals are rigid solids.
 
• Most of the metals react with oxygen to form metal oxides.
 
• This is one of the reasons that metals get corroded.
 
• Oxides of metals are basic in nature.
 
• Metal oxides react with acids very easily.
 
• Examples of metals:- Sodium, Potassium, Calcium, Iron, etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__****Non-Metallic Properties:**

 
• Non-metals are dull in appearance.
 
• They are brittle and thus, shatter when hammered.
 
• They are bad conductors of heat and electricity.
 
• They don't show the property of ductility, which means they can't be drawn into wires.
 
• They are not malleable or can't be changed into sheets.
 
• They have low densities.
 
• They can be solid, liquid or gas at room temperature.
 
• They don't produce rich sound when hit on any surface or they are not sonorous.
 
• Non-metals do not react with acids.
 
• They are generally light in weight.
 
• Non-metal oxides are molecular substances that form acidic solutions.
 
• They tend to form anions of oxyanions in an aqueous solution.
 
• They do not have any lustre or shine in themselves.
 
• Oxides of non-metals are acidic in nature.
 
• Non-metal oxides react with bases and form the salt.
 
• Examples of non-metal:- Hydrogen, Chlorine, Nitrogen, Carbon, etc.

questions.question: Who was the first ruler of Ilbari dynasty (Delhi Sultanate)?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Qutubuddin Aibak** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **first Dynasty** of the **Delhi Sultanate** was the **Ilbary Dynasty,** also known as the** Slave Dynasty, Mameluq Dynasty, or Ilbari Dynasty.**
 
• Only three of the nine rulers of this dynasty, **Qutb-ud-din Aibak, Iltutmish, and Balban**, were slaves during their early lives and the last two has been manumitted by their masters long before gaining **sovereign powers.**
 
• **Qutub-ud-Din Aibek**, a **slave of Muhammad Gori **and commander of his army formed the **Ilbary Dynasty.**
 
• The beginning of the **Sultanate of Delhi** and the **first dynasty** of the **Sultanate **is recognized as **Qutub-ud-Din Aibek’s** acceptance of **sovereign powers** in **1206.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__** Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq:

 
• He was also known as Ghazi Malik.
 
• Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq was the founder of the Tughlaq dynasty.
 
• This dynasty was also known as the dynasty of the Qaraunah Turks.
 
• He was the first sultan of Delhi who took up the title of Ghazi or slayer of the infidels.
 
• He made policies for the Construction of canals and the formulation of a famine.
 
• He started the barter system or sharing of crops.
 
• He built the city of Tughlaqabad near Delhi and made it his capital.

Iltutmish (1211-1236):

 
• ​He completed the famous Qutab Minar in Delhi.
 
• He shifted his capital from Lahore to Delhi.
 
• The Mongol policy of Iltutmish saved India from the wrath of Ghengis Khan.
 
• ​He was the real founder of the Delhi sultanate.
 
• He ruled from 1211 to 1236 AD.
 
• He introduces the Iqta system and made it hereditary.
 
• He also introduces Chalisa (a group of 40 noble people).
 
• He introduces two coins:
 
 
• Silver coin - Taka
 
• Copper coin - Jital
 
 

Razia Sultan (1236-1240):​

 
• She was the first female ruler of India.
 
• Her term was full of revolts.
 
• On October 13, 1240, she was killed by her kin. 

50:T

questions.question: What does 'L' stand for in the LPG strategy of 1991?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Liberalisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **LPG reforms of 1991** refer to the economic reform policy based on **Liberalisation, Privatisation, and Globalisation**.
 
• The letter **'L'** stands for **Liberalisation**, which aimed at reducing **government control** over industries and encouraging **private sector participation**.
 
• Liberalisation involved the removal of **industrial licensing (License Raj)**, reduction in **import tariffs**, and easing of regulations to promote economic efficiency.
 
• The reforms were introduced in **July 1991** under the leadership of **Prime Minister P. V. Narasimha Rao** and **Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh** in response to a severe **Balance of Payments crisis**.
 
• Other options, such as Legislative, Landmark, and Liquid, are unrelated to the economic reform terminology of 1991.
 
• ***Hence, the correct option is 4.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Privatisation (P)**

 
 
• Transfer of ownership and management of **public sector enterprises** to the private sector.
 
• Aimed at improving **efficiency** and reducing the fiscal burden on the government.
 
 
 
• **Globalisation (G)**
 
 
• Integration of the Indian economy with the **global economy**.
 
• Encouraged **foreign direct investment (FDI)** and international trade.
 
 
 
• **Impact of LPG Reforms**
 
 
• Shift from a **closed economy** to a more **market-oriented economy**.
 
• Acceleration of **GDP growth** in subsequent decades.
 
• Expansion of sectors like **IT**, **telecommunications**, and **services**.

questions.question: Which of the following peaks is at the highest altitude in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3.**__ 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nanda Devi** is the** second-highest peak in India after Kangchenjunga **(8,586 meters or 28,169 feet), which is located on the border of India and Nepal. However, **Nanda Devi is the highest peak located entirely within India**.
 
• 
 
The mountain is part of the Nanda Devi National Park, which is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site.** The park is known for its **diverse flora and fauna, **including several endangered species such as the snow leopard and the Himalayan musk deer.

 
 
• 
 
The name** "Nanda Devi"** comes from** Hindu mythology,** where Nanda is the name of a** goddess and Devi means "divine" or "goddess"** in Sanskrit. The mountain is considered sacred by the locals and is an important pilgrimage site for Hindus.

 
 
• 
 
**Nanda Devi has two main peaks**, **Nanda Devi East and Nanda Devi West.** The mountain was first climbed in **1936 by a British team led by Bill Tilman and Noel Odell.** Since then, it has been climbed several times by different teams from around the world.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Namcha Barwa **is a mountain located in the** eastern Himalayas**, in the **Tibet Autonomous Region of China**. It has an **elevation of 7,782 meters (25,531 feet)** and is considered one of the most beautiful mountains in the world due to its unique shape and stunning surroundings.

 
 
• **Namcha Barwa** is also known for its challenging climbing routes, and many mountaineers have attempted to reach its summit. However, the mountain's remote location and difficult terrain make it a dangerous climb, and many attempts have been unsuccessful.
 
 
 
• **Kamet is a mountain **located in the** Garhwal region of Uttarakhand state in northern India**. It is the **second-highest mountain peak in the region, with an elevation of 7,756 meters (25,446 feet). **
 
 
• **​**Kamet is part of the **Zanskar Range**, which is a subrange of the Himalayas.
 
 
• Kamet was first climbed in** 1931 by a British expedition led by Frank Smythe.** Since then, it has been climbed numerous times by various expeditions. The mountain is considered a challenging climb due to its height and difficult terrain.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Makalu** is the** fifth highest mountain peak in the world**, located in the **Mahalangur Himalayas range of the Himalayas**.
 
 
• It has an elevation of** 8,485 meters (27,838 feet) **and is situated on the border between **Nepal and Tibet.**
 
• **Makalu** is considered to be one of the most challenging peaks to climb, with technical difficulties and extreme weather conditions making it a formidable climb.
 
• The first successful **ascent of Makalu was made in 1955 **by a French team led by Jean Franco. Since then, numerous climbers have attempted to climb the mountain, with varying degrees of success.

questions.question: What was the main reason for the defeat of Sirajuddaulah at the Battle of Plassey?

options.text: Britishers cut the food supplies of Sirajuddaulah forces compelling them to surrender.
Forces led by commander Mir Jafar never fought the battle.
Sirajuddaulah's prime minister misinformed the locations of Britishers.
Britishers knew the secret way to enter Sirajuddaulah's palace.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Forces led by commander Mir Jafar never fought the battle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Battle of Plassey:-

 
 
• When **Alivardi Khan died in 1756, Siraj Ud-Daulah became the Nawab of Bengal.**
 
• The Company was worried about his power and keen on a puppet ruler who would willingly give trade concessions and other privileges.
 
• So it tried, though without success, to help one of Siraj Ud-Daulah's rivals become the nawab.
 
• An infuriated Siraj Ud-Daulah asked the Company to stop meddling in the political affairs of his dominion, stop fortification, and pay the revenues.
 
• After negotiations failed, the **Nawab marched with 30,000 soldiers **to the English factory at Kassimbazar, captured the Company officials, locked the warehouse, disarmed all Englishmen, and blockaded English ships.
 
• Then he marched to Calcutta to establish control over the Company’s fort there.
 
• On hearing the news of the fall of Calcutta, Company officials in Madras sent forces under the command of Robert Clive, reinforced by naval fleets.
 
• In 1757, Robert Clive led the Company’s army against Siraj Ud-Daulah at Plassey.
 
• One of the main reasons for the defeat of the Nawab was that the forces led by Mir Jafar, one of Siraj Ud-Daulah's commanders, never fought the battle.
 
• Robert Clive had managed to secure his support by promising to make him nawab after crushing Siraj Ud-Daulah.
 
• The Battle of Plassey became famous because it was the first major victory the Company won in India. 
 
• After the defeat at Plassey, Siraj Ud-Daulah was assassinated and Mir Jafar made the nawab.
 
• The Company was still unwilling to take over the responsibility of the administration.
 
• Its prime objective was the expansion of trade. If this could be done without conquest, through the help of local rulers who were willing to grant privileges, then territories need not be taken over directly.
 
• When Mir Jafar protested, the Company deposed him and installed Mir Qasim in his place.
 
• When Mir Qasim complained, he in turn was defeated in a battle fought at Buxar (1764), driven out of Bengal, and Mir Jafar was reinstalled.

questions.question: Who was the Viceroy of India when Morely-Minto Reforms were introduced?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Minto**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Morely-Minto Reforms__

 __
 
• The **Indian Councils Act 1909** was an act of the** British Parliament that introduced a few reforms in the legislative councils and increased the involvement of Indians (limited) in the governance of British India.**
 
• It was more commonly called the **Morley-Minto Reforms after the Secretary of State for India John Morley and the Viceroy of India, the 4th Earl of Minto.**
 
• The legislative councils at the Centre and the provinces increased in size.
 
• Indians were given membership in the Imperial Legislative Council for the first time.
 
• **It introduced separate electorates for Muslims. **
 
• The members could discuss the budget and move resolutions.
 
• They could also discuss matters of public interest.
 
• They could also ask supplementary questions.
 
• No discussions on foreign policy or on relations with the princely states were permitted.
 
• **Lord Minto appointed (on much persuasion by Morley) Satyendra P Sinha as the first Indian member of the Viceroy’s Executive Council.**
 
• Two Indians were nominated to the Council of the Secretary of State for Indian Affairs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Lord Minto-II (1905-1910):

 
 
• He was the Viceroy of India when the **Muslim League was formed.**
 
• **The Surat Split in the INC took place in the year 1907 AD. **
 
• Swadeshi Movement also took place during his period apart from the formation of the All India Muslim League in 1906.
 
• It was founded in the year 1906 by Aga Khan and Nawab of Dacca, Nawab Salim Ullah in Dacca.
 
• It was formed to promote Muslim interests in British India and enjoyed the patronage, the British.

• It is a part of the annual **Rath Yatra festival.**
 
• **Rath Yatra involves** the ceremonial procession of the deities** Jagannath, Balabhadra, and Subhadra on chariots.**
 
• **Chera Panhara is a special ritual that takes place during the Rath Yatra procession.**

questions.question: Which of the following is a tough, porous and black substance, and almost a pure form of carbon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coke**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Coke is a tough, porous, and black substance that is almost a pure form of carbon.**
 
• It is obtained by heating coal in the** absence of air to remove volatile compounds, leaving behind a carbon-rich solid.**
 
• **Coke **is commonly used as a **fuel in industries like steelmaking, where it is used as a reducing agent to remove impurities from iron ore.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bitumen**

 
 
• **​**It is also known as **asphalt is a black, sticky, and highly viscous liquid or semi-solid form of petroleum.**
 
• It is commonly used in the construction industry for** road surfacing, roofing, and waterproofing.**
 
• **Bitumen contains carbon, but it is not a pure form of carbon.**
 
 
 
• **Coal tar**
 
 
• **​**It is a black, **viscous liquid **that is produced during the distillation of coal.
 
• **It contains a variety of organic compounds, including polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs).**
 
• Coal tar has been used in the past for medicinal purposes and as a component in the production of dyes, but it is also a known human carcinogen.
 
 
 
• **Coal gas:**
 
 
• It is also known as town gas is **a flammable gas that is produced by heating coal in the presence of air or steam.**
 
• **It is primarily composed of hydrogen, methane, and carbon monoxide, with small amounts of other gases.**
 
• While coal gas does contain carbon, **it is not a tough, porous, or black substance.**

questions.question: 'Elelakkkaradi' is a tribal dance form of which Indian state?

__
 
• **Elelakkaradi is a tribal dance **form that is native to the** Wayanad district of the Indian state of Kerala.**
 
• The Elelakkaradi dance is performed by the **Kurichiya tribe, **which is a tribal community that lives in the forests of Wayanad.
 
• The dance is traditionally performed during the** festival of Onam,** which is a major harvest **festival celebrated in Kerala.**
 
• The dance is performed by a group of men who wear traditional** Kurichiya attire, which includes a long cloth wrapped around their waist and a turban on their head.**
 
• **The dancers carry wooden sticks or poles in their hands and move to the beat of the traditional drums called chenda and thappu.**
 
• The dance is characterized by energetic and synchronized movements, with the dancers forming circles and moving in a coordinated manner.
 
• The** Elelakkaradi dance** is believed to have** originated as a form of martial arts training for the Kurichiya warriors, and it is still regarded as a symbol of their strength and courage.**
 
• Over time, the dance has also become a form of cultural expression and a way to celebrate the community's heritage and traditions.

questions.question: 'SVANidhi se Samridddhi' programme launched in 2022 is associated with the Ministry of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Housing and Urban Affairs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• PM SVANidhi is an acronym that stands for Prime Minister Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi.
 
• It is a public-sector initiative that will be implemented in June 2020.
 
• Its goal is to give microcredit to street sellers afflicted by the COVID-19 outbreak.
 
• Initial operating capital of up to Rs 10,000 would be supplied to vendors.
 
• A vendor will receive a 7% interest subsidy if the loan is repaid early or on schedule. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

__
 
• M/s Quality Council of India (QCI)__ has been appointed as implementing partner for the program.
 
• Under this scheme, the complete profile of each PM SVANidhi beneficiary and their family members will be prepared.
 
• The benefits of the various eligible central schemes will be extended to the beneficiaries based on the profiled data.
 
• In the first phase,125 cities have been selected for the program.
 
• Prior to the complete roll-out, the MoHUA will run a pilot program in six cities-
 
 
• Gaya, Indore, Kakching, Nizamabad, Rajkot, and Varanasi
 
 
 
• The States/ UTs will have the option to extend their respective State/UT-specific welfare schemes to the beneficiaries under PM SVANidhi.

questions.question: Who among the following is the co-founder of Darpana Academy of Performing Arts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mrinalini Sarabhai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The co-founder of the **Darpana Academy of Performing Arts is Mrinalini Sarabhai.**
 
• **Darpana Academy of Performing Arts** is an institution in India that focuses on training in **various art forms, including dance, theatre, music, and puppetry.**
 
• **Mrinalini Sarabhai and her husband, Vikram Sarabhai,** founded the **Academy in 1949 in Ahmedabad, Gujarat.**
 
• Mrinalini Sarabhai was a renowned Indian classical dancer and choreographer who dedicated her life to the promotion and preservation of traditional Indian art forms.
 
• **She was born on May 11, 1918, in Kerala**, India, and began her training in **Bharatanatyam, a form of classical Indian dance, at a young age.**
 
• **Mrinalini Sarabhai** is one of the foremost personalities in Indian classical dance. She was trained in Bharatnatyam, Kathakali.
 
• She performed extensively both in India and abroad and was the recipient of many awards and honours, **including the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan, two of India's highest civilian honors.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pt Birju Maharaj **is an **Indian classical dancer and choreographer, known for his Kathak performances and contribution to the art form.**
 
• **Uday Shankar** was an** Indian dancer and choreographer, considered as the father of modern Indian dance and known for blending Indian classical dance with Western ballet.**
 
• **Mallika Sarabhai and Mrinalini Sarabhai** are both** Indian classical dancers and choreographers, with Mallika specializing in Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi, and Mrinalini in Bharatanatyam and Kathakali.**
 
 
• **Both have also been involved in social activism and cultural education.**
